questions.question: Remdesivir

parts.text: What is its mechanism of action?
What other 2 viruses (other than SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV) has it been shown to have activity in animal studies?

questions.model_answer:
a) Mechanism of action: remdesivir is a prodrug of an adenosine nucleotide analogue; after intracellular metabolism to its active triphosphate form, it is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase into the nascent viral RNA chain, causing delayed chain termination (evading initial proofreading by the viral exonuclease).
b) 2 other viruses shown to have activity in animal studies (other than SARS-CoV/MERS-CoV): Ebola virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (Nipah virus and Marburg virus are also accepted answers).
questions.beyond_mandell: Remdesivir preclinical/animal model antiviral spectrum data - not covered in a static Mandell chapter given the null pagefile.

parts.text: Besides the S protein, list the other 3 structural proteins
What is the mechanism of action for Remdesivir
Name two viruses that Remdesivir may be effective in treating as shown in animal models

cohort_answer.text: Proteins: E protein (envelope); M protein (membrane); N protein (nucleocapsid). Remdesivir MOA: It is a prodrug, nucleoside analog, inhibits viral replication by inhibiting RNA dependent RNA polymerase enzyme, inserting itself into RNA product and stalling RNA synthesis. Other viruses: Other coronaviruses (Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus), Ebola, Marburg (Filoviruses)

questions.question: You see an 80 year-old patient with COVID-19 who is unvaccinated. His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation. His medications include Aspirin and Rivaroxaban. He is deemed high-risk for progression to severe disease and is being considered for Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir.

parts.text: What are the specific mechanisms of action of Nirmatrelvir and Ritonavir?
In what adult population would the does of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir need to be adjusted?
The patient is a candidate for Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir. What is another consideration based on his medical history?

questions.model_answer:
a) Mechanisms of action: Nirmatrelvir is a SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CL protease/Mpro) inhibitor, blocking cleavage of the viral polyprotein and preventing viral replication. Ritonavir has no direct antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2; it is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that is co-administered as a pharmacokinetic booster to slow the hepatic metabolism of nirmatrelvir, raising and sustaining its plasma concentrations.
b) Population requiring dose adjustment: patients with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73m2) require a reduced dose; the drug is not recommended in severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe hepatic impairment.
c) Other consideration based on his history: significant drug-drug interactions - ritonavir is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and will markedly increase rivaroxaban levels (a CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein substrate), raising bleeding risk; this interaction requires holding/adjusting the anticoagulant or choosing an alternative COVID therapy, and other home medications should also be reviewed for CYP3A4-mediated interactions.
questions.beyond_mandell: Health Canada/FDA product monograph for nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) - drug interaction and renal dosing data.

questions.question: Unvaccinated 80 year old has COVID infection. He also has significant AF and is on Aspirin and Rivaroxaban.

parts.text: What is the mechanism of both ritonavir and Nirmatrevlor in Covid
What patient population requires dose adjustment
Patient is a candidate. What other considerations to factor in based on his medical history?

questions.model_answer:
a) Mechanisms: nirmatrelvir directly inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CL protease), blocking viral polyprotein processing and replication; ritonavir has no direct anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity but acts as a CYP3A4 inhibitor to boost/sustain nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations.
b) Population requiring dose adjustment: moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73m2) - reduced dose required; not recommended in eGFR <30 or severe hepatic impairment.
c) Other considerations given his history: ritonavir's strong CYP3A4 inhibition will significantly increase rivaroxaban exposure, raising bleeding risk - requires holding or adjusting anticoagulation (or interacting medication review), given his atrial fibrillation and anticoagulant/antiplatelet regimen.

questions.question: COVID-19

parts.text: What are the three structural proteins other than the spike protein?
What is the mechanism of action of Remdesivir?
What are two other viruses for which Remdesdivir has shown in-vitro activity?

questions.model_answer:
a) Envelope (E) protein, Membrane (M) protein, and Nucleocapsid (N) protein.
b) Remdesivir is a nucleotide (adenosine) analogue prodrug that is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) into the nascent viral RNA chain, causing delayed chain termination and inhibiting viral RNA synthesis.
c) Two other viruses with demonstrated in-vitro activity: Ebola virus and MERS-CoV (also respiratory syncytial virus in some studies).

parts.text: Mechanism of nirmatrelvir and ritonavir
When to adjust dose
Considerations in case of 80 yo male not vaccinated and diagnosed with COVID-19, on Xarelto and ASA for Afib, wanting to give nirmatrelvir/ritonavir - what are considerations in this case

cohort_answer.text:
Mechanism: Nirmatrelvir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor of the main protease (3C-like protease/nsp5), preventing processing of polyprotein precursors and inhibiting viral replication. Ritonavir is a booster with no independent antiviral activity that boosts plasma levels of nirmatrelvir.
When to adjust dose: CrCl >60: 300/100mg BID. CrCl 30-60: 150/100mg BID. CrCl <30: not recommended, but risk of harm is low with a 5-day course; can try 300/100 day one then 150/100 daily days 2-5, or 150/100 daily x5 days (well tolerated). Dialysis: 300/100 day one, then 150/100 daily days 2-5. Mild liver impairment: proceed. Severe liver impairment: not recommended.
Considerations for the 80yo case: Category X interaction - avoid combination of Paxlovid and Rivaroxaban. Ritonavir boosting can increase serum levels of Rivaroxaban, combination not recommended. Can consider Remdesivir instead, which does not have this interaction.

questions.question: 80yo dude is unvaccinated and has A fib, is on ASA and rivaroxaban. He gets the COVID. You are asked about starting him on nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid).

parts.text: Name the mechanism of these drugs
In what population is a dose reduction required?
Given his comorbidities above, what other management considerations are needed?

cohort_answer.text: Mechanism: Nirmatrelvir blocks the activity of the SARS-CoV-2-3CL protease, an enzyme required for viral replication; coadministration with ritonavir slows metabolism of nirmatrelvir so it remains active longer and at higher concentrations. Dose reduction population: eGFR 30-59 mL/min. Other considerations: CYP3A substrates - for medications highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance and potentially harmful at elevated levels, coadministration is contraindicated (includes alfuzosin, amiodarone, colchicine, clozapine, lurasidone, lovastatin, rivaroxaban, salmeterol, simvastatin, triazolam); if symptomatic can consider Remdesivir; COVID vaccine series and booster after recovery; counseling on warning symptoms and rebound

parts.text: Name 4 viral etiologies of gastroenteritis and 2 methods to detect them.

questions.model_answer: Viral causes of gastroenteritis: (1) norovirus, (2) rotavirus, (3) adenovirus (enteric types 40/41), (4) astrovirus (also sapovirus). Detection methods: (1) stool PCR (multiplex GI PCR panel/RT-PCR), (2) stool antigen enzyme immunoassay (EIA).

parts.text: 3 proteins aside from Spike protein
1 approved treatment for Mpox
Remdesivir treatment efficacy as per animal models

cohort_answer.text:
3 proteins: Envelope; Membrane; Nucleocapsid.
Approved treatment for Mpox: Tecovirimat (Tpoxx) - potent inhibitor of an orthopoxvirus protein required for formation of an infectious virus particle, essential for dissemination within an infected host. (Cidofovir has in vitro activity against monkeypox virus and shown effective against lethal monkeypox virus challenge in animal models.)
Remdesivir efficacy in animal models: In a study of 12 macaques, 6 treated with Remdesivir and 6 not; of the 6 treated only 1 developed dyspnea vs all of the untreated. Outpatient treatment: 4/246 (1.6%) treated arm vs 21/252 (8.3%) placebo arm required a medical visit. Inpatient treatment: 1062 randomized to remdesivir or placebo; median recovery time 10 days vs 15 days; mortality at day 15: 6.7% vs 11.9%; mortality at day 29: 11.4% vs 15.2%.
